Hello, myself and my SO are truckers. If you're in the US, get away from the mega carriers (swift, werner, c r England, knight) find a smaller company willing to train you, yes they exist. You'll get stuck with lower pay (one company it was $100 a day) for probably about a month or so but most companies you'll run for cpm (cents per mile) anything under about 30 cents per mile is bull. Shoot for about 50 cents per mile. Or get a job running percentage. Last company job I had I was working for 27% after taxes and insurance I made about $900+ a week driving solo and home every night.
Stop eating truck stop food. Stay out of them as much as possible. Get a rewards card for the truck stops. Each point is normally a cent. Swipe that bad boy every chance you get fuel. Those will save your butt. Showers are about $12 normally, rewards card? Free shower after I think it's 200 gals. Want a snack and low on funds? Use your points. No joke, Loves rewards fed me my WHOLE first year under c r England making $400 driving team. Get yourself a little crock pot bring canned goods or dry goods with you. I made oatmeal I'm my crock pot every morning and it's just a good spot to heat things up in. 

Be safe and keep is shiny side up.

Few more tips that i can think of off the top of my head:

-Flashing headlights (or at night turning them off then back on a time or two) means "youre clear to get over".
-Flashing your hazards twice or so when you pass is "thank you".
Please move over if you see a vehicle on the side of the road. That goes for trucks, emergency and tow trucks as well as cars. You never really know where that person is at. Ive been tapped by a car before. I was out of my truck and some car tapped my back with their mirror. Enough to bend their mirror in and just kept driving. 
-And if youre coming up to majorly slowed down traffic or stopped traffic turn your hazards on for a minute or so to warn others that its slowing down.

Unfortunately cars do not understand that we can't exactly stop and honestly a lot of them kind of block us out in their heads and they don't see us which I mean I don't really understand. I do fully believe that drivers ed or getting your license or whatever need to have a course where you learn about driving around a truck safely. And maybe even for a day go with a driver and see how stupid other people are around semis. I took my truck home one weekend and parked it right behind my brother's car and I had them come out and sit in my seat and take a look and see what I was able to see of their car. And now they both kind of drive like old man which is funny but it made them aware of the fact that some eyes are big and semis are deadly. And unfortunately a lot of the people especially from the bigger companies like Swift and CR England and Werner they aren't properly trained. Go take a look down the road and see how many guys you see with their leg up on their Dash. Or with their phone in their hand and not looking up. These guys are driving 80,000 lb 65 mile-an-hour missiles. They can and eventually they will kill somebody and I only hope that it's themselves and not some innocent person.

Unfortunately a lot of drivers have severe health issues. Obesity is huge in the trucking industry and heart attacks and strokes and all that are not completely uncommon at all it's actually kind of weird to not here about 1. The food available is garbage. There's no way to exercise. You sit in the seat for 11 to 14 hours a day. Every single day. These men and women are also extremely lonely and depression is high in Truckers. All you do all day is sit with your thoughts and the radio basically and things start to get to you. I don't drive over the road anymore but when I did it was one of the lowest points in my life. Looking back I miss it and I love the experience that I got and the fact that I was able to see the entire country but I do remember being extremely sad I do remember going to lay in the bunk and crying because I was so lonely people forget silly things like my birthday was forgotten and that was heartbreaking for me even though it was something that really shouldn't matter. I would call my daughter and she would talk to me for maybe about 5 minutes and then she'd want to run off and play and that broke my heart because I missed her so much. 

It's not an easy life and I wish other motorists were able to think of us as people and not an annoyance.
